findings: Native Script retains only primitive strings plus owned input bytes. Runtime inventory/refcount lifetime, initialized partial construction, and last-release unlink/free are coherent; external Script references must retire before runtime destruction.

Root FD creates the actual complete input; children inherit only after FD initialization. Filename/compile failure releases inherited owners once. Bytecode takes Script and position storage only after successful object allocation, clearing FD ownership.

Actual CJS bookkeeping root holds the original body Script; presentation text does not substitute for source provenance. Compiler metadata finalizes after the lexer and before child bytecode construction.

Captured actual frames, no-PC frames, synthetic frames and native frames initialize provenance explicitly. Actual bytecode captures and clones take independent Script references; every publication/failure/legacy temporary cleanup either moves or retires that one reference.

Raw native getters perform no public property lookup or guest conversion. Invalid outputs remain untouched. Source-line allocation respects existing pending entry; UTF-16 line/column, CR/LF/LS/PS and sourceURL precedence were read against exact V8 bodies.

Script primitive roots require no new object GC mark edge; existing captured-frame object roots remain marked. Native and serialized bytecode initialization keep new fields null until their owning producer publishes them.

Partial-construction accounting finding is corrected: Script block is always counted; input block/bytes are counted only after actual input allocation. The exact one-edit successor reverses to the reviewed original and matches the current complete C digest.
